rationale: A unanimous, text-and-structure-driven opinion is most likely assigned by the Chief to himself or to a careful institutional writer (Kagan/Barrett) to emphasize the transaction-specific limits of §§11 and 12(a)(2) and avoid turning the Securities Act into a marketwide antifraud regime. Separate concurrences are most likely from Justices emphasizing either strict textualism/history (Thomas/Gorsuch) or practical remedial concerns about direct listings while agreeing the fix lies with Congress/SEC (Sotomayor/Jackson).
